daten.text: Towards the end of October, we released a small balance patch using our new Backend Tunables system, adjusting The Executioner and The Good Guy. After working through your feedback and watching both of them in action, we’d like to further refine those changes. First, let’s get a quick recap of what the Backend Tunables system even is. Put simply, it’s a system that allows us to put small balance changes in your hands quicker, without having to wait for full patch releases. Currently, the system lets us make adjustments to many of our Killers (we’re adding support for more over time) and basekit values. While add-ons and perks aren’t currently supported, this is something we have planned for the future. Now, what’s changing today?  The Executioner: Increased the delay between each segment of Punishment of the Damned to 0.015s (was 0.001s) Dev note: The previous reduction to 0.001s made it a little too efficient, especially when paired with the Iridescent Seal of Metatron add-on. This is a great example of why we intend to add add-on support to Backend Tunables, because sometimes, basekit changes will end up synergizing more than we expected.  The Good Guy: Decreased the time to Scam

Whether you were able to tune in live (thanks!) or you're dropping by to get a tl;dr, we're here to give you a recap of some highlights from today's community stream:  MMR UPDATE As you may remember, back in 10.1.0, we updated how MMR is calculated. While kills and escapes continue to be an aspect of MMR calculations, they are no longer the only thing used to calculate these values. Now, we also factor in a wide range of actions that help progress the game – think, emblems. Of course, certain aspects of the MMR have stayed the same. Namely, Killers keep their individual MMR ratings, Survivor share their MMR, matchmaking prioritizes wait times over exact MMR matching, and MMR gains/losses are calculated by comparing Killers and Survivors against each other in a match. Since making this change in 10.1.0, we've been keeping a close eye on this system and recently noticed that Survivors' Altruism wasn't giving as much MMR as it should have. To make sure altruistic play is correctly rewarded, we made an adjustment to our MMR system earlier this week (thanks to the adjustable elements of the algorithm), increasing this value. We'll continue to keep a close eye on how this impacts players

Greetings, Fog Dwellers. Today we wanted to talk to you about some of the perk changes (spoiler alert: 58 perks are changing) and content that you can expect in the next PTB, as well as the reasonings behind them.Back in update 9.6.0, we added Diminishing Returns to the game. You may have noticed that this feature did not ship with exponential balance changes to accompany it; we wanted to ease players into the change, monitoring the impact on perk selection first, while we watch to see if any issues arise before making further changes. We feel that now is the time. Our ultimate goal is to update effects that bypass or are minimized by Diminishing Returns, and to buff gameplay effects that can safely be affected by Diminishing Returns to allow players to play around with builds and perks that aren’t picked often. Overall, we will have 26 perks affected by these changes. daten.text: A new Dead by Daylight anti-cheat trial is testing Denuvo's protection tool, but Behaviour Interactive makes clear there will be no DRM. Read the full story on PCGamesN: Dead by Daylight is now testing Denuvo, but "will not include" its anti-piracy DRM

Last week, we announced our plans to kick off our Anti-Cheat Trials initiative, and today it's here!Starting today, we will be trialing Denuvo's Anti-Cheat solution. Note that this does not and will not include anything related to DRM, as Denuvo Anti-Cheat is different from Denuvo Anti-Piracy. Another look at the difference between the two: What we ARE trialing: Denuvo Anti-Cheat A tool that detects cheats in-game, identifying people who try to get unfair advantages before they can disrupt fair play What we ARE NOT trialing: Denuvo Anti-Piracy Tools that prevent the cracking and unauthorized access of game content  In case you missed it, here's what you can expect:Anti-Cheat Trials are exclusive to Steam and cross-play will not be impacted.We’re continuously testing the compatibility and performance of each anti-cheat provider to ensure you have a seamless experience. Compatibility with Steam Deck and Proton has been tested and will continue to be supported.The first time you launch the game during the Anti-Cheat Trial, you will be prompted to install Denuvo Anti-Cheat. Greetings Fog Dwellers! Recently, we shared a survey asking for your thoughts on anti-cheat in Dead by Daylight. One message came through loud and clear: you feel we could be doing more. We hear you and are taking action to bolster and invest in our anti-cheat and security efforts. Put simply, we want you to have the best possible in-game experience, and that means fewer cheaters! While this is just one of many steps in our ongoing commitment to fair play, your involvement and feedback will play a huge part in guiding what comes next.  Beginning next week on September 2nd, we’re kicking off our Anti-Cheat Trials initiative as we investigate how different anti-cheat providers improve your in-game experience. What does this mean for you? Over the coming months, we will be running limited-time trials of these providers’ tools, directly in-game on PC, as we gauge their ability to flag cheating behaviour. By comparing your feedback and overall feelings with hard data from each trial, it’ll help us find a solution that works best for Dead by Daylight and for you, our community.  Next week’s Anti-Cheat Trial – beginning September 2nd – spotlights Denuvo’s anti-cheat solution.
